page.title: Agency Content Operations: How to Choose and Run It
page.description: A practical guide to picking an agency for content operations, covering workflow stages, tool stacks, staffing models, and the questions that reveal real capability.
page.h1: How do you choose content operations?
page.definition: Agency content operations is the end-to-end system an external partner runs to plan, produce, publish and measure content on your behalf, covering intake, briefing, production, review, approval, publishing and reporting with named owners at each stage.
page.quick_answer: Pick an agency that shows a seven-stage workflow with one owner per stage, uses a shared calendar tool, and can hand you a sample run of show and reporting dashboard from a past engagement.

sections.h2: What workflow stages should the agency own end to end?

blocks.p: A credible agency maps every piece of work through seven stages, each with a single owner and a tangible output: intake, brief, production, review, approval, publishing, reporting.

ul: Intake: request form captures goal, audience, format, deadline and approvers
Brief: structured document in Google Docs or Notion with key messages, SEO targets and distribution plan
Production: assigned writer, designer or producer works in Asana, Monday.com or Airtable
Review: tracked changes and comments in the same doc, limited to two rounds
Approval: named stakeholder signs off in the workflow tool before publish
Publishing: scheduled in WordPress, Webflow or HubSpot with UTM tags applied
Reporting: GA4 and HubSpot dashboard delivered within five working days of publish

sections.h2: Which tool categories must the agency already use?

blocks.p: The agency should operate your preferred stack or bring a proven equivalent across calendar, briefs, publishing and analytics.

sections.h2: How do you verify the agency can hit realistic timelines?

blocks.p: Ask for a recent example that shows the actual calendar from approved brief to live URL.

ol: Long-form article: five to ten working days, most time spent in review
Webinar production: three to four weeks from brief to live, including rehearsal and backup stream test
Summit or online conference: six to eight weeks, with venue AV and platform locked before agenda final
Replay delivery: within 24 to 48 hours after the event ends

sections.h2: What staffing model fits your volume and complexity?

blocks.p: Match the agency team structure to your event type and publishing cadence.

ul: Simple webinar: one producer handles run of show, speaker brief, rehearsal, live moderation and backup stream
Summit or hybrid event: show caller, speaker manager, moderator and platform operator as minimum crew
Ongoing content pipeline: dedicated content strategist, writer, designer, editor and analytics owner, or a blended producer who covers multiple roles

sections.h2: How is the feedback loop built into the contract?

blocks.p: A working feedback loop means every stage has an approval gate and a documented hand-off, not an informal email thread.

ul: Intake to brief: requestor approves the brief before production starts
Production to review: creator submits draft with a changelog
Review to approval: reviewer returns annotated doc within two working days
Approval to publish: stakeholder clicks approve in the workflow tool, triggering the publish queue
Publish to reporting: agency delivers performance dashboard on a fixed cadence, weekly or monthly

sections.h2: What conversion proof should the agency show before you sign?

blocks.p: Ask for a redacted dashboard that ties a content piece or event to a downstream metric the business cares about.

ul: Webinar: registrants to marketing-qualified leads to pipeline contribution
Article: organic sessions to newsletter sign-ups to demo requests
Summit: attendees to sales-accepted opportunities within 90 days
Community program: active members to referral revenue or retention uplift

faq.q: What is the typical cost model for agency content operations?
faq.a: Agencies usually charge a fixed build fee for the workflow setup plus a monthly retainer for ongoing production, reporting and optimisation. Day rates apply for scoped consulting assessments only.

faq.q: How long does it take to onboard an agency onto our existing tools?
faq.a: Two to three weeks for a repeat format; the agency maps your current Asana, HubSpot or WordPress configuration, builds the intake form, and runs a pilot piece through all seven stages.

faq.q: Can the agency work on the platform we already use for webinars?
faq.a: Yes. West Peek Productions produces on Zoom Webinars, Microsoft Teams, ON24, StreamYard or any platform you already licence, and can help you choose if you are evaluating options.

faq.q: What deliverables should we expect for a produced webinar?
faq.a: Run of show, speaker brief and rehearsal, branded slide template and lower thirds, live producer, Q&A moderation, backup stream, edited recording and short clips for social distribution.

faq.q: How do we measure whether the agency is improving our content velocity?
faq.a: Track cycle time from approved brief to publish, revision rounds per piece, on-time publish rate and team capacity utilisation. A first plan runs 90 days to establish a trend before adjusting targets.
